raw: 48.1 Evidence-Driven Analysis of Threat Information Sharing for ICS (arXiv 2025)[^77]
teaching_note: The inspected arXiv v3 is dated 27 January 2026, despite the inherited 2025 heading; it analyzes three cases, 196 procedure examples across 79 techniques and 22 malware families, and nine advisories [@ageint077]. Its representation and technical-detail findings concern that selected corpus and extraction method, not a causal field trial proving that all ICS sharing is ineffective. In a completed synthetic worksheet, an observable 'tag Q changed' is representable as text but lacks units, provenance, and operating mode; the reviewer records 'interpretable: unknown; releasable: not yet determined; operational conclusion: hold'. A later card identifying Q as a classroom label resolves interpretation only, not source permission or detection efficacy.
title: Evidence-Driven Analysis of ICS Threat Sharing: Versioned Corpus Study

teaching_note: An information-sharing organization provides a community and exchange context, not automatic authority to redistribute every contribution; the inherited SSDF/DevSecOps sources do not establish the named ISACs' current membership or service rules. A fictional producer supplies record R1, 'two missing toy telemetry messages', marked TLP:AMBER+STRICT with an additional 'exercise team only' restriction; the reviewer removes an unnecessary site-like label, keeps the original restriction, records authorized recipients A and B and a next-class review trigger, and obtains their paper acknowledgments [@official_first_tlp_v2]. Recipient B's request to send even a sanitized excerpt to an external group is held until explicit source permission; sanitization is not permission to downgrade. A corrected R2 attributes the gap to planned maintenance, so the reviewer withdraws R1's attack inference, records A/B receipt of the correction and cessation of reuse, while preserving only the authorized minimized exercise record.
title: ISACs: E-ISAC, WaterISAC, FS-ISAC

teaching_note: Distinguish a CISA recommended practice from a statute, a mandatory sector requirement, and an organization-specific approval; general secure-development guidance is not a universal sharing licence [@ageint307]. TLP indicates redistribution boundaries, not classification, encryption requirements, copyright permission, privacy exemption, or collection authority [@official_first_tlp_v2]. For TLP:GREEN, FIRST supplies a default cybersecurity/defense community when none is defined, but a proposed recipient outside a clear boundary or a mixed-source record with conflicting restrictions requires clarification rather than unilateral widening. Source restrictions and applicable rules remain binding even when a format can encode the record.
title: CISA Frameworks for Critical Infrastructure

teaching_note: NERC CIP applicability requires the particular standard/version, responsible entity, covered system or facility, jurisdictional approval and effective status, and relevant exclusions; 'critical infrastructure' alone is not an applicability test [@official_nerc_cip_standards]. In fictional record E, an electricity entity's covered-system status and standard version are missing, so the reviewer holds any mandatory-control claim; in record W, a water-only teaching diagram supplies no basis to import NERC obligations. The inherited SSDF and DevSecOps references provide software-development context, not evidence of NERC applicability. Neither completing this worksheet nor adding a control label establishes compliance.
title: NERC CIP Standards

raw: 48.5 IDS/IPS for OT Networks: Dragos, Claroty, Nozomi, Armis
teaching_note: An IDS identifies observations for review; an inline IPS may affect traffic, so false positives, latency, and failure behavior have different safety and availability implications. In a paper-only comparison, fictional monitor M reports a benign maintenance event, while fictional blocker P would interrupt that same event: the review records an alert-quality problem for M and a potential availability consequence for P, not permission to deploy either. Vendor names are examples, not independent performance evidence or endorsements; the inherited development sources do not validate their products. No blocking, tuning, live traffic collection, or production response is performed.
title: IDS/IPS for OT Networks: Dragos, Claroty, Nozomi, Armis

raw: 48.6 Honeywell ICS Security: Defense in Depth[^218]
teaching_note: Defense in depth combines control functions rather than counting products: prevention constrains exposure, detection reports observations, protective systems limit hazardous conditions, and recovery addresses restoration under authorized engineering control [@ageint218]. A fictional paper map gives monitor M and historian H a common data source; agreement between them is a common-cause blind spot, not independent confirmation. The correct reviewer answer is to mark the dependency and unknown coverage, not certify resilience. These distinctions support a classroom architecture critique, not a production recovery procedure; apply Section [@sec:analytic-workflow] to separate the proposed control from any claimed effect.
title: Honeywell ICS Security: Defense in Depth
